results.proposal_summary: The Elsie Initiative Fund (EIF), supported by Canada and administered through the UNDP Multi-Partner Trust Fund Office, launched its Fourth Programming Round on 9 October 2025 to increase the meaningful participation of uniformed women in UN peace operations. The fund supports Troop/Police Contributing Countries (T/PCCs) and Participating UN Organizations (PUNOs) through two modalities: Flexible Project Funding (FPF) and MOWIP Barrier Assessments. The Letter of Interest stage, which was the first mandatory application step, is now closed; the page currently serves invited applicants proceeding to full proposal development. Grant amounts are denominated in USD but no specific ceiling is stated. The call is global in scope, targeting countries contributing uniformed personnel to UN peacekeeping missions.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The call addresses gender equality and women's participation in peace operations, which has partial overlap with ILO's decent work and equality mandate, but its primary focus on uniformed military/police personnel in peacekeeping is outside ILO's core labour and employment policy mandate.

results.proposal_summary: The Phortify Internship (Traineeship) Grants Pilot Call (DIGITAL-2024-ADVANCED-DIGITAL-07-KEYCAPACITY) is a student mobility grant programme launched by Phortify under its Funding Framework, published on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal for visibility purposes only. The call supports individual students—both those enrolled in Phortify Master's Degree Programmes and non-degree-seeking students participating in Phortify-labelled internships—at partner institutions including AFS (Germany), ICFO (Spain), TU/e (Netherlands), WUT (Poland), and FSU (Germany). Grants range from €600/month (up to 6 months) to €2,000 lump sums depending on the partner, with a total call budget of €91,800. Eligible applicants must be nationals of EU Member States or associated/cooperating countries under the Digital Europe Programme. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis from 4 February 2026 until 3 February 2027 via the Phortify website. The ILO is not an eligible applicant as the call targets individual students only.
results.ilo_match_evidence: This call funds individual student internships in photonics/digital technologies and has no substantive connection to the ILO mandate of labour standards, employment policy, social protection, or decent work.

results.proposal_summary: This call, funded under the EU CERV Programme (2021–2027) and managed through Poland's Equal Rights Programme, provides experience sharing grants to support peer learning between two Polish civil society organisations (CSOs) working on anti-discrimination, hate speech/hate crime, rule of law, or human rights. Grants range from approximately EUR 2,315 to EUR 4,600 (PLN 10,000–20,000), with a total budget of approximately EUR 69,460 (PLN 300,000). Eligible applicants and partners must be non-profit CSOs established in Poland with specific legal forms (foundations, associations, church legal persons, rural housewives' circles, ordinary associations) and registered at least 12 months before application. Eligible activities include study visits, joint workshops, job shadowing, traineeships, expert exchanges, and joint initiatives. Applications are evaluated on a rolling basis with four cut-off dates, the final being December 18, 2026. The ILO is not eligible as it is not a Polish CSO, and the grant maximum is well below the USD 50,000 threshold.

results.proposal_summary: Switzerland's State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) launched a third call for proposals on 28 May 2026 to support Ukraine's reconstruction by co-financing investment projects involving the Swiss private sector. The call targets Swiss companies with an established presence in Ukraine, inviting them to submit proposals for the construction and reconstruction of production and/or operations facilities in Ukraine. The federal government provides up to CHF 50 million in co-financing, with individual project grants ranging from CHF 3 million to CHF 10 million; companies must contribute at least 50% of project costs. Projects are selected through a two-stage process by a joint Swiss-Ukrainian committee, with selection concluding by spring 2027 and implementation to follow. The submission deadline was 20 September 2026, which has now passed. The ILO is not eligible as only Swiss private sector companies qualify.

results.proposal_summary: The Common Fund for Commodities (CFC) 29th Call for Proposals, which closed on 1 October 2026, sought project proposals from commodity-sector agribusinesses and SMEs operating in CFC Member States. The CFC provides funding exclusively through loans and debt instruments, with a maximum of USD 1.5 million for regular projects and up to USD 300,000 under a Fast-Track procedure. The call focused on transformative projects empowering smallholder farmers, supporting climate-smart practices, strengthening biodiversity, and enabling access to high-value markets, with a thematic alignment with the VACS initiative. Eligible applicants must demonstrate at least a 3-year track record with audited financials; start-ups, humanitarian, educational, and medical projects are excluded. The 30th Call is expected to be announced soon.
results.ilo_match_evidence: While the call references smallholder income, gender indicators, and decent work (SDG 8), its primary purpose is private-sector agribusiness debt financing rather than technical assistance, labour standards, or social protection programming within ILO's mandate.
